measuredBy: american-hotel rework lane, 2026-10-13: read off the rectified panorama crops of `landmark-brief.ts --pand=0363100012168734` (artifacts/landmark-briefs/american-hotel/, Gemeente Amsterdam panoramas CC BY 4.0) with the metre grid of `elevation-grid.ts`, and pitched views cut from the full panoramas with `pano-look.ts` (artifacts/landmark-briefs/american-hotel/tower/). Values in `inferred` lists are not visible in any crop.
frame: s = metres along the photographed wall from its viewer-left corner (the crop's left edge); y = metres above the 3DBAG ground after the crop's `yShift`. On the builder's ring-edge frame: t = s - s0 (american-hotel-walls.ts prints s0 per edge). The curved canal block uses u = arc length along ring edges 31-37 from the start of edge 31 (u = s - 0.21 on w03, u = s + 17.34 on w05).

w02-53.what: Marnixstraat corner pavilion (NE): two narrow side bays with small blue-star gablets either side of a centre bay under the big pointed gable; a three-light round-arched window two storeys tall at the ground, a three-arch loggia on four columns, a disc balustrade, two storeys on three axes, a row of six small arched windows, a blue zig-zag ceramic frieze and the gable with its lunette, star and finial

frieze.pattern: blue zig-zag and diamonds on buff

inferred: loggia depth 1.5 m (the back wall is in shadow)
relief depth of the frieze and stars (0.05-0.1 m)

w03-220.what: the curved 1927 Leidsekade block (dark brown brick): granite plinth with barred basement windows, segmental ground windows under striped (cream / orange) arch hoods, an arcade storey of paired round-headed windows between piers carrying caryatid figures, the piers and a hanging bracket per bay carrying a projecting arched corbel table, a brick band, three storeys of canted stone-framed oriels, the parapet
w03-220.crop: w03-220.jpg (+ w03-220.thumb.jpg aimed view for registration)
w03-220.registration: the rectified crop is a plane through a curved wall: the arcade, which stands ~0.4 m proud, reads 0.5-1.3 m off the ground windows in s. The aimed view w03-220.thumb.jpg shows each ground window centred under a bay, the caryatid piers over the brick piers between them; that is what the builder uses.
inferred: oriel centres are the mean of w03 (s 5.3, 9.4, 13.5) and w05 (s 3.2): the rectified curve smears them by up to 0.6 m
caryatids are drawn as standing figures (body, head, hands), not sculpted

w05-227 + w06-234.what: the buff Jugendstil gable front on the Leidsekade (ring edges 38 + 39, 10.25 m): paired windows with fanlights, five-arch arcade under ring tracery, stone balustrade, windows alternating arched / narrow, a dormer row of four arched windows, the blue zig-zag band and the big gable with a lunette
w05-227 + w06-234.registration: both 2017 crops are taken from the canal (camera below the quay): the curved block's arcade crown and oriel base read 0.9-1.0 m higher than in the 2023 street crop w03 (8.45 / 10.4); all heights here are shifted by -0.95 m
inferred: the two bays on edge 38 are behind the cruise kiosk at the ground: ground storey drawn like edge 39's
gable apex from the 3DBAG roof planes

w08-233.what: the corner bay between the gable front and the round tower: entrance under a segmental arch, rusticated piers with stacked blocks, pierced stone balustrade, arched windows

tower.what: the round corner tower: brick shaft with groups of narrow windows and the AMERICAN HOTEL mosaic panel, a cornice, an open arcaded belfry drum, a square stone clock stage with gilt dials on each face, a flat cap

plan.source: 3DBAG LoD2.2 tower walls 33-47, 200, 323-325 (polygon x -10.7..-4.5, z 15.9..20.7) enclosed by the drum

inferred: stage heights from the pitched views scaled to the 3DBAG top (39.4 m), +-0.4 m
dial detail (gilt sunburst): a gold disc with hour marks

w01-143.what: Leidseplein front: Bar Americain canopy, entrance arch and three segmental cafe windows on a 6.05 m pitch, a balustraded first-floor loggia with striped awnings in its arches, an eaves balustrade, two storeys on seven axes, stepped dormer gables

loggia.arches: one segmental arch per cafe bay

inferred: upper rows behind trees: axes over the arches and between them (the 2025 leaf-off spec)
